_comment: W1-T2698 ratchet baseline: per host class, the set of credential-reach target ids a worker-shaped subprocess can READ. test/credential-reach-probe.test.ts attempts each target with `test -r` (never `cat`), resolves refusals from settings/worker.json's own deny rules, and FAILS BY NAME on any id that is reachable here and absent below. THE SET MAY ONLY SHRINK. Re-capturing it upward is not a remedy — it is the widening the ratchet exists to refuse; the sanctioned path for a deliberate new reach is to record it in the SAME PR with the reason in the PR body. An entry the probe no longer reaches is reported as closable and the PR that closed it drops the line. A host class with no entry below FAILS rather than passing vacuously: the first run on a class is what records it, and a silent pass on an unmeasured host is the exact family of result CLAUDE.md's positive-control rule refuses.
_classes_recorded: ci-ubuntu and unknown-linux are MEASURED. `mini` (the operator's macOS host) and `azure-container` are deliberately ABSENT: neither has run this probe, and writing a guessed set for them would be a claim about a machine nobody measured. The first run on each records it.
_finding: ungoverned:operator-claude-json is REACHABLE on unknown-linux and is the finding this task was filed to surface, not a failure of it. The operator's ~/.claude.json carries oauthAccount and is named by NO deny rule in settings/worker.json and NO grant in WORKER_HOME_SYMLINKS — it falls between the two tables. W1-T2699 is the shard that shrinks it; this baseline is what makes the shrink observable.
